counterexample: Take the point (1,0) on the x-axis Ox. Under L(x,y)=(x,x+y), it maps to L(1,0)=(1,1). But (1,1) does not satisfy the claimed image-line equation x+y=0, since 1+1=2. In fact, every point (t,0) maps to (t,t), so L(Ox) is y=x, not x+y=0.
assessment_summary: Steps 0001–0007 are justified: L is the invertible linear map with matrix [[1,0],[1,1]], hence an affine transformation. The first definite error is step 0009, which identifies the image of the x-axis incorrectly. The intended conclusion remains true after replacing x+y=0 by y=x, since that line forms an acute angle pi/4 with the y-axis, but the proof as written contains a false step.
